Known for his {{convert|7|ft|5|in|cm|adj=on}} wingspan, he played [[college basketball]] for the [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State Aztecs]].{{cite news|first=Bernie|last=Wilson|title=No. 6 Aztecs hope for rest, not rust, during long layoff|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2020/03/09/no-6-aztecs-hope-for-rest-not-rust-during-long-layoff/111411862/|work=[[USA Today]]|date=9 March 2020|access-date=21 October 2020}} ==High school career== Mensah grew up playing soccer in Ghana. At the age of 13, he began playing basketball after being recruited to play in a tournament. Mensah was spotted by Kwaku Amoaku and moved to the United States to attend [[Prolific Prep]]. In August 2017, he averaged 13.8 points and 7.4 rebounds per game for Team Africa in the Adidas Global Nations event. Mensah transferred to [[Findlay Prep]] before his senior season. Rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], Mensah committed to playing college basketball for [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] in October 2017, choosing the Aztecs over [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite news|first=Mark|last=Zeigler|title=SDSU lands another hoops recruit from Ghana|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/sd-sp-sdsu-nathan-mensah-20171004-story.html|work=[[The San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=4 October 2017|access-date=10 November 2020}} ==College career== As a freshman at San Diego State, Mensah averaged 5.6 points and 5.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web|first=Yaw|last=Mintah|title=San Diego's Mensah diagnosed with blood clots|url=https://www.basketballghana.com/2020/01/23/san-diegos-mensah-diagnosed-with-blood-clots/|website=BasketballGhana.com|date=23 January 2020|access-date=10 November 2020}} On 28 December 2019, Mensah requested to be substituted during the second half of a game against [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly]], due to shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with a [[pulmonary embolism]], forcing him to miss the remainder of the season.{{cite news|first=Mark|last=Zeigler|title=Aztecs' Nathan Mensah has 'outside chance' of returning this season|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2020-01-17/sdsu-aztecs-basketball-nathan-mensah-pulmonary-embolism-blood-clot-mountain-west|work=[[The San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=17 January 2020|access-date=10 November 2020}} Mensah averaged 6.9 points and 6.8 rebounds per game as a sophomore.{{cite news|first=Tron|last=Johnson|title=Countdown Of The Best Mountain West Basketball Players For 2020-21|url=https://mwwire.com/2020/11/10/countdown-of-the-best-mountain-west-basketball-players-for-2020-21/2/|work=Mountain West Wire|date=10 November 2020|access-date=10 November 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 8.1 points and 6.1 rebounds per game.{{cite news|first=Sean|last=Paul|title=Matt Bradley headed to San Diego State|url=https://mwwire.com/2021/04/13/matt-bradley-headed-to-san-diego-state/|work=Mountain West Wire|date=13 April 2021|access-date=16 June 2021}} Mensah was named [[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] Defensive Player of the Year as a senior as well as Honorable Mention All-Mountain West,{{cite press release|title=Mountain West Reveals 2021-22 Men's Basketball All-Conference Teams|url=https://themw.com/news/2022/3/8/athlete-awards-mountain-west-reveals-2021-22-mens-basketball-all-conference-teams.aspx|website=TheMW.com|publisher=[[Mountain West Conference]]|date=8 March 2022|access-date=8 March 2022}} and helped lead the Aztecs to their first Final Four and national championship game. ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets / Greensboro Swarm (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Mensah joined the [[Charlotte Hornets]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]. On 5 September 2023, he signed with the Hornets,{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-four-players|website=NBA.com|date=5 September 2023|access-date=8 September 2023}}{{cite news|first=Mark|last=Zeigler|title=Undrafted, SDSU's Nathan Mensah signs deal with NBA's Hornets; many Aztecs foes picked|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2023-06-23/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-nathan-mensah-nba-draft-charlotte-hornets-exhibit-10-contract|work=[[The San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=23 June 2023|access-date=30 June 2023}} but was waived on 21 October, prior to the start of the season.{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive Brown, Hunter, Mensah|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-brown-hunter-mensah|website=NBA.com|date=21 October 2023|access-date=24 October 2023}} Eight days later, he signed with the [[Greensboro Swarm]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Greensboro Swarm Announce Training Camp Roster and Coaching Staff for 2023-24 Season|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-swarm-announce-training-camp-roster-and-coaching-staff-for-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=29 October 2023|access-date=5 November 2023}} On 14 December, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Hornets{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign Nathan Mensah To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-nathan-mensah-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=14 December 2023|access-date=14 December 2023}} and the next day, he made his NBA debut in a 112–107 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. On 2 March 2024, he was waived by the Hornets{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign Nathan Mensah To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-nathan-mensah-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=2 March 2024|access-date=2 March 2024}} and two days later, he returned to Greensboro.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Greensboro Swarm Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Greensboro-Swarm/45/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=5 March 2024}} ===Austin Spurs (2024)=== On 28 September 2024, Mensah signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]],{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Spurs Sign, Waive Nathan Mensah|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/nathan-mensah-signing-with-spurs.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=13 October 2024|access-date=13 October 2024}}{{cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs Officially Sign Recent Hornets Player|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/san-antonio-spurs-officially-sign-recent-hornets-player-mensah|website=SI.com|date=29 September 2024|access-date=30 September 2024}} but was waived on 13 October. On 29 October, he joined the [[Austin Spurs]].{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2024 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/austin-spurs-announce-2024-training-camp-roster/n-6160743|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=29 October 2024|access-date=3 November 2024}} Mensah played his debut game with the Austin Spurs on November 8, 2024 in a 128 - 117 win over the [[Osceola Magic]] where he recorded 6 points, 8 rebounds, 1 assist and 2 blocks in 17 minutes.https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2052400004/ He would only play for 12 games during the Tip - Off Tournament, averaging 5.4 points ad 7.0 rebounds in 21.0 minutes per game. This statline greatly helped the Spurs as they had a 9 - 3 record in those 12 games. However, Mensah would not stay with the Austin Spurs for their regular season as he would play his final game with them on December 10 against the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]]. The Spurs won the game 124 - 112 with Mensah recording 6 points, 5 rebounds and 2 blocks.https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2052400179/ ===Olympiacos (2024–2025)=== The day after his final game with the Austin Spurs on 11 December 2024, Mensah signed with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]], replacing the injured [[Moses Wright]].{{cite web|title=Στα «ερυθρόλευκα» ο Νέιθαν Μενσά|url=https://www.olympiacosbc.gr/el/news-el/announcements-el/10852-sta-erythrolefka-o-neithan-mensa.html|website=OlympiacosBC.gr|date=11 December 2024|access-date=12 December 2024|language=Greek}} On 23 April 2025, Mensah was released from the Greek club. In 9 games, he averaged 3.9 points and 3.1 rebounds in 12 minutes of play. ===Büyükçekmece Basketbol (2026)=== On April 9, 2026, he signed with [[Büyükçekmece Basketbol|ONVO Büyükçekmece]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite Instagram |user=buyukcekmecebsk |postid=DW61RpSiFGG |title=Ailemize Hoş Geldin Nathan Mensah |date=April 9, 2026}} ===Petkim Spor (2026–present) === On July 27, 2026, he signed with [[Petkim Spor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=Petkimspor |number=2081652167627165755 |title=Ailemize hoş geldin Nathan Mensah}} ==Career statistics==
